title: Developing Tomorrow's Perioperative Leaders Today: A Comprehensive Leadership Development Program.
text: Developing Tomorrow's Perioperative Leaders Today: A Comprehensive Leadership Development Program.. Frontline nurse leaders face challenges as the health care landscape and workforce evolve, creating unique learning needs. Executive leaders in the Nursing Perioperative Services Institute at a regional health care system identified structured leadership development training as an opportunity to increase nurse leader job satisfaction, improve retention, and create a leadership pipeline for novice and emerging nurse leaders in perioperative services. The program leads created a 10-month leadership development program based on organizational needs assessments and nationally established nurse leader competencies. The program incorporated didactic training, action learning, and mentoring. Program evaluation was guided by the Kirkpatrick Model's levels of evaluation. Sixteen participants in the first two cohorts self-reported high satisfaction with program content and presenters, increased confidence in leadership competencies, and improved job satisfaction. Participant-led quality improvement projects demonstrated improved department outcomes affecting patient safety, waste or cost reduction, staff engagement, or department efficiency in alignment with organizational goals.

title: Discovery of Virulence Attenuator of Chromobacterium violaceum CV026 From Marine-Derived Fungus Aspergillus ochraceus LSD-13 by Inhibiting Quorum Sensing and Destroying Biofilm.
text: Discovery of Virulence Attenuator of Chromobacterium violaceum CV026 From Marine-Derived Fungus Aspergillus ochraceus LSD-13 by Inhibiting Quorum Sensing and Destroying Biofilm.. Targeted quorum-sensing (QS) represents a promising approach to combat multidrug-resistant infections. In this study, an undescribed pyrazine derivative 5-isobutyryl-1,4-dihydropyrazine-2,3-dione (1) together with three known compounds (2--4) were isolated from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus ochraceus LSD-13. Compound 2 was a potent virulence attenuator of Chromobacterium violaceum CV026 with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 32 µg/mL. At sub-MIC, compound 2 significantly suppressed the production of QS-controlled phenotypes: violacein, N-acyl homoserine lactone, chitinase, and extracellular polysaccharide. It also reduced biofilm formation by 73.3% at 1/2 MIC, a phenotype confirmed by scanning electron microscopy. Furthermore, compound 2 inhibited swarming motility in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistic investigations revealed that compound 2 downregulated the expression of QS-associated genes (cviR, vioA, vioC). Molecular docking demonstrated that compound 2 has a strong binding affinity for CviR protein with -6.8 kcal/mol, suggesting a competitive antagonism of the native CHSL ligand. These findings highlight compound 2 as a promising QS inhibitor with therapeutic potential against C. violaceum CV026.
